object_description: narrow monolithic disk-like building with cantilevered front facades
design_condition: The building opens the western space toward the tracks while its eastern extension contains the parking exit and a small tapering green area; the jury wished it shifted eastward.

positive.statement: Accommodating all required orders in one building is convincing and promises an exciting economic contribution.
The cantilevered structure and articulated front facades create a strong address with an inviting spatial effect.
The western placement suggests an actual train station square.
The stacked apartments provide attractive, easily furnished units and flexible commercial spaces.
Sliding walls promise a high degree of flexibility in the room layout.
The strict and efficient building grid supports attractive apartments and flexibly divisible commercial spaces.
The simplicity of the structure is captivating and reaches its greatest quality in its object-like implementation.

negative.statement: The twisting of the protruding building parts appears formal and rather alien to the proposed architecture.
The central urban space is overloaded by densely packed functions and overlapping traffic flows.
The proposed pocket park may not be needed at this location.
The two-story ramp system is too broad, too complicated and correspondingly expensive.
Visibility conditions in the underground facility are sometimes critical.
The consistent design approach makes it impossible to respond adequately to the varied urban environment and functional conditions.
The proposal has clear deficits in the overlay of complicated traffic functions, the underground car park and the open-space arrangement.
